title: The Gold Ring Dropped in the Deep Well (TE)
summary: Akbar drops a diamond ring into a deep, narrow stone crevice where hands cannot reach. Birbal retrieves it using grease and string. [TE]
full_text:
While inspecting the ancient stone fortifications of Fatehpur Sikri, Emperor Akbar leaned over an ornamental parapet and his diamond ring slipped off, falling directly into a deep, narrow vertical fissure between two massive stone foundation blocks.

The crevice was nearly fifteen feet deep, but barely the width of two fingers.

Akbar peered down into the dark crack: the diamond glinted far below, but no human arm could reach it. Royal blacksmiths tried lowering iron hooks, but the crevice was jagged and the hooks caught on the stone edges. Others proposed chiseling away the historic masonry, but Akbar forbade damaging the palace wall.

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'Can you retrieve my ring without chipping a single stone?'

Birbal smiled: 'Certainly, Your Majesty. All we need is a lump of cow wax, a heavy lead fishing sinker, and a spool of silk twine.'

Birbal walked to the palace kitchen and took a fist-sized ball of soft, sticky beeswax mixed with pine pitch. He pressed the sticky wax firmly around the bottom of the heavy lead sinker, leaving a broad, flat, adhesive base.

Birbal tied the silk twine securely around the top of the weight.

Lowering the wax weight carefully down into the narrow crevice, Birbal used a small hand mirror to reflect a beam of sunlight directly into the crack, illuminating the diamond ring resting on the dark ledge below.

Guiding the string with steady, gentle hands, Birbal lowered the sticky wax until it rested firmly atop the diamond ring.

Birbal let it sit for two minutes, pressing down gently so the warm wax molded tightly around the gold band and the diamond.

Then, with smooth, unhurried precision, Birbal pulled the silk string upward.

Up, up, up came the lead weight—and sticking firmly to the bottom was Emperor Akbar's sparkling diamond ring!

Birbal peeled the ring from the wax, cleaned it with a linen cloth, and presented it to the Emperor with a low bow.

The courtiers cheered in delight. Akbar slipped the ring onto his finger, exclaiming: 'Birbal, you solve with sticky wax and patience what twenty blacksmiths could not accomplish with iron hooks!' Akbar rewarded Birbal with a purse of gold.
